observations: body L1-L12: the end of the entry on pp. 288 and 289, begun on p. XXV. «Kitāb al-manshūrāt», «distantiis magnitudinibusque», «Introductorio» and «libris intervallorum celestium corporum» are italic; «al-Bīrūnī», «Aristarchi», «Abū» «Ma‘shar», divided between L6 and L7, «Ibn Rosteh» and «al-Farghānī» are letter-spaced; «Al-Battānī» (L3), at the head of a paragraph, is not.

body L1-L5: several t's print without their cross-stroke, like an l («hausit», «titulum», «vertit», «Battānī», «memorati», «satis», «osten-», «dunt», «praeter»); they are transcribed as the words read. The p of «parum» prints broken.

body L5-L6: the title of Aristarchus' book in Greek. The θ of «μεγεθῶν» is the curly form of this type (ϑ) and the κ of «καὶ» the open form (ϰ); «ἡλίου» has the rough breathing. The accented η of «σελήνης» prints with a short upright stroke after it, not transcribed, as on pp. XXI-XXII and XXV.
body L7: a speck in the left margin beside the line (0.8 pt) is not transcribed.

body L7-L9: the passage of the Introductorium keeps its spellings «celestium», «lune», «terre» and its numbers between stops, «.128.» and «.94.»; «[sic]» after «vere» is Nallino's. The lines of the quotation after the first open with a guillemet. The upper arm of the opening bracket of «[sic]» prints faintly.

body L10-L12: 128 094 : 3818 = 33.55, and 33 1/2 1/20 = 33.55, as printed; this is the least distance of the Moon, in radii of the Earth, in the table of Barhebraeus on p. XXV (L39). The e of «Lunae» (L10) prints like a c; a dot at half the height of the letters between «quam» and «al-Farghānī» (L11, 0.6 pt) is a speck; the e of «seu» (L12) prints filled.

body L13-L15: the entry on p. 305, n. 1, «305» bold. «Pauli Ale-» «xandrini» is letter-spaced; «adnotator Schaton», «adnotator ab Andrea Schatone editus», «Rudimenta in doctrinam de praedictis» and «natalitiis» are italic. In the Greek title the κ of «ἀποτελεσματικήν» is the open form (ϰ), and its accented η prints with the short upright stroke after it.

body L16-L26: the entry on p. 318, «318» bold; «Suter» is letter-spaced and «datae urbis» (L21) italic. A dot after «p. 88)» (0.7 pt, below the baseline; the stops of the line measure 1.8 pt) is a speck.
body L17: «ab aequatorem» is printed so, for «ad aequatorem»; its b prints broken.

body L18-L26: the figure stands at the right of lines 18 to 26, which are set beside it in a narrow measure. It is redrawn from measurements of the print: the meridians from the pole P through the given city A and through Mekkah B down to the equator, traced along the middle of their printed strokes, and the equator as a straight line; the arcs CA and BA of great circles, traced in the same way; the braces of the latitudes, φ′ from A to the equator and φ from B to the equator; the bold italic letters P, A, C and B, the angle λ−λ′ at P, and the word aequator, printed in a script italic, in the italic of the text. A mark (4.2 by 2.4 pt) at the right of the foot of φ′ is a speck and is not drawn.

body L22-L26: the formulas are checked. In the triangle PAB the side PB is 90° − φ, the colatitude of Mekkah, and the angle P is λ − λ′, the difference of longitude; the rule of sines gives sin PAB = sin PB sin P : sin AB = sin (λ − λ′) cos φ : sin distantiae. AC is perpendicular to the meridian PA, so that PAB = PAC + CAB = 90° + azimuth and sin PAB = cos azimuth. The formula of t. I, p. 318, has φ′ in place of φ, as L26 says.

body L23, L25: the formulas are centred in the measure of the lines beside the figure. «PAB», «PB» and «AB» are italic in the first formula; «PAB» is roman in L24. The minus signs of λ − λ′ are printed with a dash (9.5 and 9.7 pt) and set as minus signs; the signs = are printed long (9.7-10.9 pt), and the plus sign of L24 is large (10.3 pt). A speck in the left margin beside L25 is not transcribed.

body L27-L28: «al-Battānī» is letter-spaced; the dash of «1°—2°» measures 9.5 pt. With modern coordinates, the rule (α) of t. I, p. 318 (sin azimuth = R sin (φ′ − φ) : sin distantiae), with the true distance, differs from the angle given by the formula of L25 by 0.8°-1.3° at Damascus, Aleppo, Mosul and Baghdad, by 1.8° at Wāsiṭ and 2.1° at al-Baṣrah, and by 0.3° at ar-Raqqah.

body L29: the title of the Addenda to the second volume, in large capitals; the face is not imitated and the line is scaled to the box of the printed line. A speck stands at the foot of the line before the title (1.8 pt), and one in the opening of the C of «SECUNDUM». The rule under the title is 63.4 pt long and 0.84 pt thick.

body L30-L37: the corrections to the second volume. The page numbers are bold, the numbers corrected and their corrections italic, with the double primes of the seconds; «31,10» is page 31, line 10. The dashes of L36 measure 10.3 and 10.2 pt. Specks around the title and between the lines of the corrections are not transcribed.
body L36: «ad nr. 4»: the 50″ stands in the day column of year 6 of the table of p. 32, and Nallino's notes (Part II, p. 207) read «40″ pro 50″ sub anno 6»; year 4 has 47″. Kept as printed.

notes_left L1-L2, notes_right L1-L2: one note in two columns with a thin rule between them, running from the left column into the right. «Albu-» «masaris Abalachi» is letter-spaced; «Introductorium in astronomiam», «octo continens libros par-» «tiales» and «c7» are italic. No stop follows «cap».
